blocks.heading: WELCOME — DAY 3
blocks.board_text:
Student Mode · Day 3 of 5

You know cloud and IAM.
Today: Networking Basics — VPC

We will cover:
• What a VPC is and why isolation matters
• Public vs private subnets
• Internet gateways and traffic paths
blocks.ren_voice: Welcome Day 3. Cloud and IAM theriyum. Inniku walls draw panrom — networking. VPC na Virtual Private Cloud: AWS-la unga private slice — enna public, enna private, traffic eppadi move aagum. EC2 and database ellam indha map-ku ulleye irukkum. Teach, board, mic check. Network open panrom.

blocks.heading: WHAT IS A VPC?
blocks.board_text:
VPC = Virtual Private Cloud.

It is your own private section of AWS's network — isolated from every other customer's infrastructure.

Without a VPC: your resources exist in shared, open space.
With a VPC: you define the walls, the doors, and who has the keys.

Four things you control inside a VPC:
• Your own IP address range
• Which resources are reachable from the internet
• Which resources are internal-only
• The traffic rules between every resource
blocks.ren_voice: VPC-nu Virtual Private Cloud — namba own private section of AWS's network. AWS-la resources create pannaa, oru open, shared space-la thozhuma pogaadhu. AWS namba-ku isolated section edukka allow pannum. Entire AWS network-a oru city-nu vachu yosinga. VPC namba-oda private property antha city-la — walls engey, doors engey, yaarukku key-nu namba decide pannuvom. IP address range namba control pannuvom, which resources internet-la irundhu reach panna mudiyum, which resources internal-only, every resource-ku traffic rules — ellam namba define pannuvom. VPC illaadhappo, database-a yaaraavathu right address-la reach panna mudiyum. VPC irundha, explicit permission illaamal yedhuvo ulla vara mudiyaadhu.

check_question.question: What is the core thing a VPC gives you that you don't have without one?
check_question.ren_response_if_correct: Exactly — isolation. Namba resources, veyra AWS customer-oda resources-la irundhu separated. Explicit permission illaamal yedhuvo reach panna mudiyaadhu. Andha isolation-taan networking-la ellathukum foundation.
check_question.ren_response_if_incorrect: Virtual Private Cloud-la 'Private'-nu oru word irukkuu — adhai yosinga. VPC illaadhappo, resources shared space-la walls illaamal irukkum. VPC kudukkurathuu isolation — namba own walled section of the network, namba allow pannaamal yedhuvo ulla varalaamilla.

blocks.heading: WHY DOES EVERY COMPANY NEED A VPC?
blocks.board_text:
Without a VPC (or with a misconfigured one):
• Your database is exposed to the internet
• Any port-scanning tool can find it in minutes
• A weak password = data breach
• This happens. Constantly. To real companies.

With a properly configured VPC:
• Database is in a private subnet — invisible from the internet
• Even if someone finds the address, the traffic is blocked at the network level
• A misconfiguration in one service does not automatically expose everything else

VPC is the first wall. Without it, every other security measure is compensating for a missing wall.
blocks.ren_voice: Theory-ku appuram yen ithu matter-nu solren. Internet-ku exposed databases — VPC isolation illaadhappo — global-a most common data breaches-la oru. Exotic attacks illai. Zero-day vulnerabilities illai. Port scanning. yaravadhu oru tool oottuvaanga, IP ranges scan pannum, open database ports-ku respond panna paakkum, one ketchitta common passwords list try pannum. Password weak-a irundha, network wall illaadhappo, minutes-la breach aagum. VPC, database-yae find panna impossible-a aakaara wall. Database VPC's private section-la irukku, internet-la irundhu reach panna mudiyaadhu. Attacker internet scan pannaa, respond pannaa oru port find panna mudiyaadhu. VPC first wall. Veyra ellam adhai vachhu katta.

check_question.question: If a VPC is missing or misconfigured, what does an attacker need to access your database — assuming they know the IP address?
check_question.ren_response_if_correct: Exactly — password mattum. Illa, database version-la known vulnerability irundha, adhaiyum kammiya. Network isolation illaadhappo, attacker-ku database-ku data-ku indha mattum thaaan barrier — database credentials. Adhu-taan VPC isolation non-negotiable-a treat pannuvaanga.
check_question.ren_response_if_incorrect: Network isolation actually enna block pannum-nu yosinga. VPC properly configure illaadhappo, database internet-la irundhu reach aanalaa, attacker-ku address ketchitta, database authentication-a maattum pass panna vendiyathu. Weak password — ulla varaanaa. VPC database-a unreachable-a panniduchu, attack surface-yae remove aaguthu.

blocks.heading: HOW A VPC WORKS — THE MENTAL MODEL
blocks.board_text:
Think of your VPC as a building:

• Public subnet = the reception area — anyone can walk in
• Private subnet = the server room — internal access only, no public entrance
• Security Group = the lock on each individual door
• Internet Gateway (IGW) = the building's main entrance from the street
• NAT Gateway = a one-way exit — internal resources can reach out, nothing reaches in

Rule:
API servers and web servers → public subnet
Databases and internal services → private subnet, always
blocks.ren_voice: Mental model solren. Namba VPC oru building. Andha building-la rendu maathiri spaces irukkum. Public subnet reception area maathiri — street-ku face pannum, yaarum front door-ku walk pannalaam. Web server or API server idha-la irukkum. Private subnet server room maathiri — public entrance illai, internal staff mattum pooglaam. Database idha-la irukkum. Internet Gateway building-oda main entrance from the street — adhu illaadhappo, traffic ulla vara mudiyaadhu, veliyey poga mudiyaadhu. NAT Gateway internal resources-ku one-way exit — database server software updates download pannalaam, ulla varaadhu. Security Groups each individual door-oda lock — which traffic each specific resource-la allow-nu define pannuvaanga. Innaikku oru rule edukkanom: databases always private subnets-la. No exceptions.

check_question.question: Your API server needs to receive requests from users on the internet. Your database stores user data. Which goes in the public subnet and which goes in the private subnet?
check_question.ren_response_if_correct: Correct — API server public subnet-la, database private subnet-la. API server internet-la irundhu requests receive panna reach panna vendiyathu. Database direct-a internet-la irundhu reach panna venam — API server mattum reach panna venam, adhu VPC-ku ulleye nadhakkum. Perfect.
check_question.ren_response_if_incorrect: Rule-a solren. Public subnet, internet-la irundhu traffic receive panna venum-na — API server. Private subnet, internet-la irundhu direct-a reach pannakoodaadha — database. API server database-a internally talk pannum, VPC-ku ulleye. Users database-a direct-a talk pannaadhu.

blocks.heading: WHAT THIS LOOKS LIKE IN THE AWS CONSOLE
blocks.board_text:
In the real AWS console:

→ Services → Networking & Content Delivery → VPC
→ 'Your VPCs' — see all VPCs, their CIDR blocks (IP ranges)
→ 'Subnets' — see all subnets, whether public or private, which AZ they're in
→ Click a subnet → 'Route Table' tab shows where traffic goes
→ 'Security Groups' — see the traffic rules for each resource
→ 'Internet Gateways' — see which VPCs have a public entrance

Route table is the proof: a public subnet's route table has a route to an Internet Gateway. A private subnet does not.
blocks.ren_voice: AWS console-la enna paappeenga-nu solren. Services → Networking and Content Delivery → VPC. Left sidebar-la 'Your VPCs' — each VPC-oda CIDR block, IP address range, paappeenga. Subnets click pannaa, every subnet — which VPC, which Availability Zone-la. Oru subnet public-a private-a-nu eppadi theriyum-na — click pannunga, Route Table tab parunga. Public subnet-oda route table-la 0.0.0.0/0 traffic-a Internet Gateway-ku route panna oru line irukkum. Private subnet-la andha route illai. Oru difference, route table-la — andha-taan subnet-a public or private-nu decide pannum, checkbox illai, label illai, actual route configuration. Security Groups separately listed, each one-oda exact inbound and outbound rules paakkalaam.

check_question.question: In the AWS console, how do you confirm whether a subnet is truly public or private — what would you look at?
check_question.ren_response_if_correct: Exactly — route table. Public subnet-la 0.0.0.0/0 Internet Gateway-ku point panna route irukkum. Private subnet-la andha route illai. 'Public'-nu label-a matter illai — route-taan matter.
check_question.ren_response_if_incorrect: Andha subnet-ku associate aana route table-a parunga. Subnet click pannu, Route Table tab. 0.0.0.0/0-ku Internet Gateway-ku route irundha, subnet public — internet traffic reach panna mudiyum. Andha route missing-na, subnet effectively private. Label peyar mattum. Route-taan reality.

blocks.heading: YOUR TURN — WHAT WOULD YOU DO?
blocks.board_text:
Scenario:
Your company's new web app is ready to deploy.
It has two components:
• An API server that handles user requests
• A database that stores user accounts and order history

You need to decide:
• Which subnet does the API server go in?
• Which subnet does the database go in?
• What Security Group rule does the database need?
blocks.ren_voice: Real deployment decision. API server-um database-um irukkum. Rendu-um VPC-ku ulleye irukkanum. Enna subnet-la each one, database-a protect panna enna security rules-nu decide panna vendiyathu. Yosinga — API server-a yaaru reach panna vendiyathu, database-a yaaru reach panna vendiyathu, adhu placement and security rules-a eppadi determine pannum?

check_question.question: Walk me through your decisions — where does each component go, and what is the key security group rule on the database?
check_question.ren_response_if_correct: Right — API server public subnet-la, internet-la irundhu HTTPS traffic accept pannum. Database private subnet-la, Security Group API server-oda Security Group-la irundhu mattum inbound traffic allow pannum — internet-la irundhu illai, veyra source-la illai. Andha rule, wall-ku ulayey oru wall.
check_question.ren_response_if_incorrect: Guide panren. API server user requests internet-la irundhu receive panna vendiyathu — public subnet. Database API server-la irundhu mattum traffic receive panna vendiyathu — private subnet. Database-oda Security Group, inbound connections API server-oda Security Group-la mattum allow pannanum — internet-la irundhu illai. Structure-a purindhudaa?

blocks.heading: WHAT HAPPENS WHEN YOU GET NETWORKING WRONG
blocks.board_text:
A real mistake that happens repeatedly:
A startup puts their RDS database in a public subnet 'for easier access during development.'

What actually happened:
• Database launched in a public subnet with a public IP address
• Security Group allowed inbound traffic on port 5432 from 0.0.0.0/0
• Launched on a Monday. Breach detected on Thursday.
• A scanner found the open port, brute-forced a weak password
• 6 months of customer data: exposed
• The database was in production the entire time

'We'll move it to private later' is how this starts every time.
blocks.ren_voice: Ithu constantly happen aaguchu. Oru startup fast-a build pannikittu irukkaa. Database public subnet-la, yen-naa developer laptop-la irundhu direct connect panna convenient-a irukkum development-la. Security Group database port-la wide open. Production-ku munnaadi tighten panna plan. Production-ku ponnaanga. Nobody database-a move pannala. Nobody Security Group update pannala. Four days piragu, oru port scanner database find panna pannuchu, weak password brute-force pannuchu, six months customer data access pannucha. Developer-oda laptop still andha same database-ku connect aagittu irundha — ippo attacker actively read pannakittu irukkaan. 'We'll move it to private later' — ithu every time-um ippadi start aaguchu. Later-nu oru later illai. Private subnet from day one. No exceptions.

check_question.question: In that scenario, what two things would have prevented the breach — name one networking fix and one Security Group fix?
check_question.ren_response_if_correct: Correct — database private subnet-la move pannaa public IP illai, internet-la irundhu reach panna mudiyaadhu. Security Group API server-oda Security Group-la irundhu mattum allow panna configure pannaa, address ketchitta kooda traffic block aagum. Rendu layers. Database effectively invisible and unreachable.
check_question.ren_response_if_incorrect: Rendu separate layers yosinga. First, subnet — database private subnet-la irundha public IP illai, internet-la irundhu reach panna mudiyaadhu. Second, Security Group — public IP irundhalum, API server-la mattum allow pannaa, brute-force attempt block aagum. Rendu layers. Rendu-um venum.

blocks.heading: QUICK CHALLENGE
blocks.board_text:
A developer on your team says:
'Can you just open port 22 to 0.0.0.0/0 on the EC2 security group? It's easier for me to SSH in.'

What do you say, and what do you offer instead?
blocks.ren_voice: Oru developer-kitta port 22, entire internet-ku, EC2 instance-oda Security Group-la open pannunga-nu solluvaanga. Port 22 SSH — server-a directly access panna use panna port. 0.0.0.0/0-ku open pannaa internet-la every IP address attempt panna mudiyum. Developer-kitta enna solluveengaa, alternative-a enna offer pannuveengaa?

check_question.question: What is your response — what do you decline, and what do you offer instead?
check_question.ren_response_if_correct: Exactly right — port 22 to 0.0.0.0/0 decline pannuveengaa, entire internet-ku attack surface create aaguchu. Alternative: AWS Systems Manager Session Manager — port 22 illaamal EC2 instance-ku terminal access kudukum. Illana SSH-ku insist pannaa, their specific IP address-ku mattum restrict panna vendiyathu, not entire internet.
check_question.ren_response_if_incorrect: Alternative-a offer pannunga: port 22 to 0.0.0.0/0 means internet-la every machine andha server-ku connect try panna mudiyum. Automated scanners ithai constantly try pannuvaanga. Safer alternative: AWS Systems Manager Session Manager — inbound port illaamal terminal access. SSH venum-nu irundha, Security Group rule their specific IP address-ku mattum restrict pannunga.

blocks.heading: HOW SWIGGY'S NETWORK IS STRUCTURED
blocks.board_text:
Swiggy — Indian food delivery, millions of orders daily:

• Order database → private subnet. No public IP. Unreachable from internet.
• API servers handling order requests → public subnet behind a load balancer
• Traffic flow: user → load balancer → API server → database (all inside VPC)
• At no point does a user request reach the database directly
• Security Groups: database only accepts traffic from API server's Security Group
• Multiple Availability Zones — if one AZ fails, traffic routes to the other automatically
blocks.ren_voice: Swiggy-maathiri scale-la eppadi structure pannaanga-nu paarkalam. Order database private subnet-la — public IP illai, internet-la irundhu reach panna mudiyaadhu, scanner-ku ever find panna mudiyaadhu. API servers public subnet-la, load balancer-oda behind — users-kitta irundhu requests receive panna pannuvaanga. Traffic flow: user request pannaanga, load balancer hit aagum, load balancer API server-ku route pannum, API server database-a query pannum. Andha chain-la user-ku direct-a database-ku path illai. Database-oda Security Group, inbound traffic API server-oda Security Group-la mattum allow pannum — veyra ondrum illai. Entire setup multiple Availability Zones-la — oru data center problem-nu irundha, traffic automatically veyra-ku route aagum. Idhu VPC networking at production scale.

lesson_summary.board_text:
What you must know after Day 3:

• VPC = your private, isolated section of AWS's network
• Public subnet = faces the internet (API servers, load balancers)
• Private subnet = internal only (databases, internal services) — always
• Security Groups = per-resource traffic rules — define exactly what is allowed in and out
• Internet Gateway = the entrance from the internet to your VPC
• NAT Gateway = one-way exit for private resources to reach the internet
• Route table = what actually makes a subnet public or private (not the label)
lesson_summary.ren_voice: Innaikku enna edukkanom. VPC namba isolated network inside AWS — explicit permission illaamal yedhuvo ulla varalaamilla. Public subnets internet-ku face pannum. Private subnets pannaadhaa. Databases always private subnets-la — exceptions illai, 'later-la move panniduvaom' illai. Security Groups each resource-a lock pannum. Route table proof — traffic actually enna ulla vara, veliyey poga mudiyum-nu solluchu, subnet-a enna-nu call pannaa. Naalaikku: EC2 and S3 — andha network-oda mela run aagura compute and storage layer.
